title: Judge PR-only commits after C0 by the pre-merge rule in check --history
summary: On a head that is not main, `athena check --history` after C0 will judge commits in merge-base(main)..head by the pre-merge rule (records-only, declared intervention, or a verified job landing). It keeps the attribution rule for commits on main. The audience is the maintainer and CI, which currently fails the required 'the full history' check on every PR.

defaults_applied.how: New tests cover the PR-branch pass, the PR-branch failure and main unchanged; cargo test and clippy stay clean.
Criteria run athena check --history on fixture branches and check the pass/fail outcome and the named commit.
The range split is fixed in the history check itself, not by skipping the check in CI.
The verifier runs cargo test on the fixture-based tests.
One change: range split, classifier move, CI fetch tweak and changelog.
The behavior is enforced by the required history check and its tests.
All changes are Rust, plus the CI YAML.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: athena-gate does not depend on athena-core (gate Cargo.toml lists data, git, score), and land.rs classify_commit already uses gate's invariant::closing_jobs. So the classifier moves into the gate and land.rs pr_commits/classify_commit delegate to it, keeping their behavior and tests.
'main' means the remote main ref (origin/main or local main) available in the checkout; if the merge base cannot be found, the check falls back to today's behavior and adds a note.
A head 'is main' when it is an ancestor of, or equal to, main's tip. Then the whole post-C0 range stays under attribution, so history on main is unchanged.

The CI change is limited to what the PR-head run needs: fetch main and athena/records so the merge base and records resolve. The existing PR-event skip of the records fetch is revisited. The checkout token persistence is narrowed to the fetch step if feasible.
Tests for the acceptance cases use the existing cutover fixture from crates/athena-core/src/test_support.rs (job 20261025-031609-k0tt), driven from crates/athena-cli/tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test on the cutover fixture creates a PR branch after C0 with a records-only commit, a declared-intervention commit and a verified job-landing commit, none named by a landing record. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli` (the new history test): `athena check --history` on that head reports no violations.

A test adds a governed-content change with no verification or intervention to a PR branch after C0. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli` (the new history test): `athena check --history` fails and the violation names that commit's sha.

A test shows `athena check --history` on the fixture's main after C0 gives the same report as before: commits on main still go through the attribution rule, and an unattributed commit on main still fails. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate -p athena-cli`.
All existing history and attribution tests and the land.rs pr_commits tests pass unchanged. Run `cargo test --workspace`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

The CI history job in .github/workflows/ci.yml has the refs it needs on a pull_request event (main, and athena/records where used) so the merge base resolves. The step comments say why. The job keeps the name 'the full history'.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that says a PR head's own commits after C0 are judged by the pre-merge rule and main's by attribution, and cites the PR #175 failure.
The pre-merge classifier has one source of truth in the gate; land.rs pr_commits delegates to it, with no duplicated rule logic.

out_of_scope: Changing the attribution rule's treatment of commits on main.
Changing branch protection or the other CI jobs (attribution, pr-head).
Re-running or repairing the cutover import itself.
departures: Higher cost and wall time than the reference: the classifier has to move across the crate boundary (gate cannot depend on core), a new fixture-based test is needed, and CI has to be checked. Verification pass is slightly lower because the CI criterion cannot be run locally.
